name: GraspNet-1Billion: A Large-Scale Benchmark for General Object Grasping
description: GraspNet-1Billion is a large-scale real-world robotic grasping dataset and 6D grasp pose estimation benchmark developed by Shanghai Jiao Tong University. Captured across 190 dense, heavily cluttered scenes containing 88 common household and industrial objects, GraspNet-1Billion comprises 97,280 RGB-D images recorded with calibrated Intel RealSense D435 and Microsoft Azure Kinect sensors. Crucially, the dataset provides over 1.1 billion analytical 6D grasp pose annotations evaluated across diverse gripper widths and friction models—representing grasp annotations per image rather than 1 billion images—along with 6D object poses, dense object point clouds, and segmentation masks.

citation.paper_title: GraspNet-1Billion: A Large-Scale Benchmark for General Object Grasping

provenance.collection_method: Robotic arm mounted multi-sensor scanning of physical tabletop object scenes using RealSense D435 and Kinect Azure sensors, followed by physics-based analytical grasp evaluation.
provenance.curation_notes: Scenes are partitioned into training, test seen, test similar, and test novel splits to benchmark zero-shot 6D grasp generalization to unseen objects.
data_sources: Original recordings at Machine Vision and Intelligence Group (MVIG), SJTU
